intended_object: A progressively measurable process: for each time t, the map (s, ω) ↦ u_s(ω) on [0,t] × Ω is measurable for the product σ-algebra B([0,t]) ⊗ F_t. Inferred from the docstring and name.
explanation: The definition requires that for every `i`, the map `(s, ω) ↦ u s ω` on `Set.Iic i × Ω` is measurable. The σ-algebra used is the product of the subspace σ-algebra on `Set.Iic i` (induced from the σ-algebra on `ι`) with `f i`. This is the textbook definition of progressive measurability. Using `Set.Iic i` in place of `[0, i]` matches the usual definition when the index set has bottom element 0, such as ℝ≥0 or ℕ, and is the natural extension to any preorder. The definition is stated for a general preorder `ι` with a measurable space structure and for a general measurable codomain `β`, which is the natural generality. Mathlib's `IsStronglyProgressive` is the strongly-measurable variant. The same file proves the two notions are equivalent for pseudo-metrizable Borel codomains, so neither one is a narrower version of the other.
